name: Kipsigis
confidence_why: Kouneli 2019, Bossi 2023 and Toweett 1975 all describe Kipsigis as a tone language and say nothing of word stress, and Rottland 1982 found no stress accent in phonemic function in his Kalenjin recordings; the only stress placement ever claimed, Tucker and Bryan's 1966 group-level "stress falls normally on the stem syllable", is read by Rottland as prominence that simply tracks high tone.

Corroborated by Toweett, Taaitta. 1975. Kalenjin nouns and their classification, with notes on phonology and a noun list appendix. MA thesis, University of Nairobi (scan). catalog_quote: Kipsigis has three phonemic tones: High (H), Low (L), and a contour high-falling tone (HL). While H and L can appear on any syllable, the contour tone is only attested on long vowels and, somewhat more rarely, on syllables with a short vowel and a sonorant coda. ... Kipsigis, like other Kalenjin dialects, exhibits a small number of tonal processes, which are all limited to interactions between adjacent tones or tones associated to adjacent morae or syllables. In other words, tone in Kipsigis is not very mobile and we never find long-distance tonal phenomena, or tones that appear far from their underlying position. Furthermore, the language has the typologically rare property of completely lacking downstep (Creider 1982). [Kouneli 2019:30-31] || Vowels only have tones in Kipsigiis. There are four main tones in Kipsigiis. [Toweett 1975:xvii]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kipsigis is described purely as a lexical/grammatical tone language (H, L, HL; mora as TBU; tonal nominative case; local sandhi). The most detailed open phonological sketch (Kouneli 2019, 17 pp.) and Toweett's 1975 Kipsigis phonology notes ('Vowels only have tones in Kipsigiis. There are four main tones..', p.xviii) say nothing about word stress or accent placement; no open source states where stress falls or that there is none.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tonal: contour HL barred on monomoraic syllables; *HL.HL repaired by mora deletion; word-final H -> L before a word-initial H.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone from elicited citation/NP forms; one sandhi rule operates across word boundaries. An explicit Kalenjin-wide 'Druckakzent' (stress accent) subsection exists in Rottland 1982 sec.5.1.3.2 (p.77-78) but could not be opened, so whether Kipsigis has a (predictable) stress accent alongside tone remains unverified here.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe Kipsigis proper (kips1239; Toweett 1975 calls it 'Kaaleenychiin (Kipsigiis)', Rottland 'Kipsikiis', older literature 'Lumbwa'); Kouneli's consultants came from three Kipsigis-speaking areas of western Kenya (Kericho region). Rottland 1982 and Tucker 1964/1966 treat 'Kalenjin' (macro-language kale1246) as a whole, Nandi-Kipsigis based; Nandi (nand1266) is already in the catalog as tonal, so a Kipsigis entry is a separate language-level node, not a duplicate.

new_statements.quote: Kipsigis is a tonal language. There are three surface tones in Kipsigis: high (H), low (L), and a contour high-falling tone (HL) (Kouneli & Nie 2021:117). H and L can appear on syllables with long or short vowels, while HL can only surface on long vowels and in some syllables with a short vowel and a sonorant coda (Kouneli & Nie 2021:117). All sequences of tones across two syllables are grammatical in Kipsigis, except sequences of contour tones (Kouneli 2019:33).

tone_statements.quote: Let us begin with some relevant phonological background on Kipsigis. There are two contrastive tone heights: H and L. HL contours are attested on heavy syllables, which include those with long vowels or short vowels plus a sonorant coda: kárâ:rán, ‘beautiful.SG’. ... LH tones never surface on a single syllable, although sequences of L and H are permitted on successive syllables. When a LH tone would otherwise surface in hiatus contexts, there is a regular flattening of LH to H
tone_statements.locator: p.415, sec. 3.1 'Across-the-board tonal polarity in Kipsigis'
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Two contrastive tone heights H and L; HL contour only on heavy syllables (also from /H-H/ on one syllable); LH banned, flattened to H. Data credited to Kouneli & Nie 2021. Topic: nominative across-the-board tonal polarity on modifiers, analysed by constraint reweighting. Nothing on Kipsigis stress.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement among the three listed works as opened: Bossi 2023 (fully read) describes a three-tone system and is silent on stress; Tucker & Bryan 1966 (snippets) give a group-level 'stress falls normally on the stem syllable' alongside three level tones; Tucker 1964 (one snippet) merely presupposes stressed syllables. The one tension is external to the list: Rottland 1982:78 (Google Books snippets held from an earlier reading, sec. 5.1.3.2 'Druckakzent') reports no evidence of stress accent in phonemic function in his own Kalenjin recordings, notes that Tucker/Bryan's stress appears correlated with high or rising tone, and says phonetically stressed syllables always carry non-low tone; that reading treats the Tucker & Bryan stem-stress statement as tone-driven prominence rather than a stress rule.

sources.citation: Sande, Hannah. 2022. Is grammatical tone item-based or process-based? Phonology 39(3): 399-442. doi:10.1017/S0952675723000106 (published online 2 Oct 2023; open access, CC-BY 4.0).
sources.quote: Let us begin with some relevant phonological background on Kipsigis. There are two contrastive tone heights: H and L. HL contours are attested on heavy syllables, which include those with long vowels or short vowels plus a sonorant coda: kárâ:rán, ‘beautiful.SG’. ... LH tones never surface on a single syllable, although sequences of L and H are permitted on successive syllables. When a LH tone would otherwise surface in hiatus contexts, there is a regular flattening of LH to H
sources.locator: p.415, sec. 3.1 'Across-the-board tonal polarity in Kipsigis'
sources.note: Two contrastive tone heights H and L; HL contour only on heavy syllables (also from /H-H/ on one syllable); LH banned, flattened to H. Data credited to Kouneli & Nie 2021. Topic: nominative across-the-board tonal polarity on modifiers, analysed by constraint reweighting. Nothing on Kipsigis stress.
